chunks: And by this chain, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and he was saying: 'Every heart that contains doubt or shirk (association) is fallen, and what is intended by asceticism in the world is to free your hearts for the Hereafter.'

key_terms.الزُّهْد: Asceticism or renunciation of the world

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of doubt or shirk in the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the validity of the heart by its purity from doubt (shakk) and polytheism (shirk), establishing that any spiritual impurity renders the heart 'fallen' or invalid. He clarifies that the asceticism (zuhd) advocated in Shia tradition is not an end in itself, but a means to detach the heart from worldly distractions, thereby preparing it for exclusive devotion to the Hereafter. This reflects the Shia emphasis on inner monotheism (tawhid al-qalbi) as the foundation of spiritual integrity.
